title: Seedling Template Greenhouse — prompt experiments and micro-bench
content:
Purpose: quick scratchpad for iterating small prompt template families (seedlings) before promoting the winners to the shared prompt bank. Keep rough notes, microbench outcomes, and failure cases here so we don't lose context.

Context / constraints:
- Target models: open-llm-16b-v2 (quantized) on dev cluster, plus hosted baseline (rwd-host-gpt4-lite).
- Token budget: 220–400 tokens per call for interactive assistant flows.
- Latency-sensitive paths: customer chat (<= 250ms tail preferred). So templates must be compact.

Naming convention I want to try: seedling-[intent]-[style]-v# (e.g. seedling-summarize-compact-v1)

Quick hypotheses to test (tracking here):
1) Anchored negative exemplar reduces hallucination in fewshot summarization (short 2–3 shot).
2) Implicit role + soft constraints ("be concise: <20 words") improves token economy vs strict format enforcement.
3) Mixing 1 positive + 1 negative exemplar better than 3 positive for borderline cases.

Experiment set A — compact summarizers (goal: factual, ≤30 words)
- seedling-summarize-compact-v1
  Prompt scaffold:
    System: "You are a concise assistant that only summarizes facts present in the input. If uncertain, say 'insufficient information'."
    Fewshots (2):
      1) Input: "Article: ..." -> Summary: "Key fact A; Key fact B."
      2) Input: "Blog: ..." -> Summary: "Main point X."
    Instruction: "Summarize in ≤30 words. Do not infer beyond text."
  Notes: start temp 0.0, max tokens 80, nucleus 0.95.
  Observations (01/22 run):
    - open-llm-16b-v2: 78% adherence to ≤30 words, but ~18% hallucination (inferred entity not present).
    - rwd-host-gpt4-lite: 92% adherence, 6% hallucination.
  Failure case examples: model invents company name when input mentions "a startup" without name.
  Quick fixes tried:
    - Add negative exemplar: "Input: 'A report about a startup' -> Summary: 'insufficient information'" (seedling-summarize-compact-v1b). Reduced hallucination to 8% on open-llm but also increased 'insufficient information' responses to 12% (acceptable trade).

Experiment set B — instruction sandwich for coding tasks
- seedling-code-explain-sandwich-v1
  Scaffold: System short role, then 1-shot example showing minimal but complete explanation and a short example code snippet. Finish with explicit step headers: "What it does | Complexity | Example".
  Observations: Good for prompts where user pastes small functions. Models were more likely to include exact code in 'Example' block. However risk: verbosity explosion if we don't bound tokens. Tried suffix instruction: "Now give result in 3 bullet points max." Reduced output length consistently.

Experiment set C — contrastive fewshot for refusal alignment
- seedling-refusal-contrast-v1
  Idea: include one positive exemplar (good refusal) + one 'bad' exemplar (over-apologetic/rambling refusal) labeled explicitly. Then final instruction: "Respond concisely and refuse only when unsafe."
  Findings: On open-llm, contrastive fewshot nudged tone (less rambling) but also sometimes toggled to over-cautious refusal. Need to try weighted priming (longer good exemplar than bad).

Logging format for failures (keeping short here):
- ID: F-20250122-01
  Prompt variant: seedling-summarize-compact-v1
  Input excerpt: "A spokesperson said" (no org name)
  Model output: "Spokesperson from Acme Corp said..."
  Type: invented-entity (hallucination)
  Mitigation attempted: added negative exemplar -> reduced but didn't eliminate.
  Next step: try explicit deny rule in system message and a final check: "Check: do you have a named entity not in input? If yes, answer 'insufficient information'."

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Run 100-sample micro-eval for each seedling at temps = {0.0, 0.2, 0.4} and record hallucination rate + brevity score.
- [ ] Add metric hooks to console project for per-prompt token breakdown so we can estimate cost impact. (See linked GH PR for instrumentation).
- [ ] Try 1 negative + 2 positive exemplars vs 3 positive on summarization.
- [ ] Try soft-format enforcement: "Output only the summary on a single line" vs rigid labels — measure compliance.

Random brainstorm ideas to preserve:
- "Anchor checklist" pattern: after model returns, append validator: 'If you included facts not in input, prefix with [INFERRED]'. This helps downstream UIs flag uncertain facts.
- Use explicit 'source attribution' slot in fewshot outputs: models often omit provenance; teaching them to put 'Source: sentence 3' helps traceability.

Notes to self / rough schedule:
- Next week: run micro-eval for compact summarizers; collab w/ Marco to wire up console metrics.
- After that: pick top 2 seedlings and push to /shared prompt bank as experimental templates. We'll keep version history.

Misc links and scraps:
- Slack thread: #prompt-garden (see message 2025-01-12 for initial idea)
- Quick eval dataset: /datasets/micro/summ-220.json (local path on dev only)

End of scratchpad. Keep it messy. If it becomes stable, migrate to a proper PRD with evaluation tables and acceptance criteria.

-- Avery
